You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer-side assessment

The Seller’s draft shifts substantial deal risk to Wattlebridge. The main concern is the combined effect of a low cap, short claim period, broad disclosure and knowledge exclusions, and provisions that may make those limits apply to every type of claim. Those terms could leave the Buyer with little practical recourse even for significant pre-Completion liabilities.

The points below are based on the Seller’s update and Disclosure Letter only; the full SPA, data room and funds-flow model should also be checked.

## Priority pushbacks

1. **Do not apply the general warranty cap or time limit to every claim.**  
   A cap of AUD 4.8 million is only 20% of the AUD 24 million price. That may be a negotiating starting point for ordinary warranty claims, but it should not cover all claims. Seek separate, materially higher or uncapped protection for fraud, deliberate concealment, title and capacity, and agreed specific indemnities. Tax, IP and other material risk areas should have tailored protection rather than being swept into the general regime. The same separation should apply to time limits: 18 months is short for issues that may emerge later. Seek longer periods for general claims and, for tax and other claims with longer discovery or statutory periods, appropriate tailored periods.

2. **Reject the de minimis and tipping basket as drafted.**  
   Under the proposal, an individual claim must exceed AUD 25,000 and aggregate claims must exceed AUD 250,000; only the excess over the basket is recoverable. That leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 of otherwise valid claims, as well as smaller claims. Seek a lower de minimis and a deductible basket (recovery from the first dollar once the basket is crossed), or at minimum materially lower thresholds. These thresholds should not apply to fundamental claims, fraud or specific indemnities.

3. **Narrow the disclosure and knowledge exclusions.**  
   Disclosure of *every* fact in the data room and public records is too broad: it risks treating a document’s mere presence as disclosure of every relevant fact or consequence. Require fair, specific disclosure in the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for the Buyer to understand the nature and scope of the matter. General data-room and public-register disclosure should not qualify warranties. Limit any knowledge exclusion to actual knowledge of specifically identified Buyer deal-team members after reasonable inquiry—not adviser knowledge, constructive knowledge or matters merely discoverable in diligence. The Seller’s own reservation that the Buyer must evaluate disclosed facts reinforces the need for specific, intelligible disclosure.

4. **Protect the Buyer against the Riverlark debt and security.**  
   The facility is approximately AUD 3.2 million, is still outstanding, and has no final discharge in the data room. A release after Completion is not adequate for a debt-free/cash-free transaction: the Buyer could inherit repayment, enforcement and security risks. Require repayment and irrevocable discharge of all related security at or before Completion, with lender evidence and delivery of release documents. Alternatively, use a robust completion-mechanics solution—such as direct payment to the lender with simultaneous release—and retain sufficient funds if any discharge document cannot be delivered at Completion. Confirm the debt is reflected in the price adjustment and funds flow.

5. **Make Bluefen consent and conditions an actual Completion condition.**  
   Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue (around 30%). The Seller has not provided final written consent or evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been met. “Reasonable endeavours” and treating consent as satisfied on receipt of a letter are not enough if conditions remain outstanding. Require the executed consent and satisfaction or waiver of every associated condition before Completion, with no adverse amendment or termination right triggered by the transaction. If not obtained, Wattlebridge should have a termination right or other agreed protection.

## Specific exposures to address

- **Ironquay IP:** The Seller’s proposed indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, but DD-004 says transfer of Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. Require evidence of cleared payment and an effective assignment/transfer of all relevant IP and materials by Completion. The indemnity should cover failure to obtain title, infringement or third-party claims, and related loss—not merely the stated payment. Verify the position independently; the disclosure itself says the open balance is not bank-verified.

- **DD-006 export/privacy incident:** This is not safely dismissed as a preliminary operational matter. The link went to an unintended external email address and may include about 1,240 records; access, scope and notification obligations remain unknown. Require full investigation and remediation, preservation of evidence, timely regulatory/individual notifications where required, and continuing disclosure. Seek a specific indemnity for losses, response costs, claims and penalties attributable to pre-Completion events, outside the general cap and basket, or another carefully negotiated risk allocation if the facts cannot be resolved before Completion. Do not treat the absence of a confirmed breach or quantified loss as proof there is no exposure.

- **DD-005 bonuses:** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from the funds flow, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. Establish whether these are seller or target liabilities, quantify all on-costs, and agree who bears them. They should be paid or specifically adjusted for at Completion, with no leakage or post-Completion surprise to the Buyer. Reconcile the funds flow to the agreed debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

- **Supplier renewals:** The three renewals total AUD 330,000 and should be reviewed together. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course commitments. Confirm their terms, timing, termination rights and accounting treatment; ensure they are included in working capital or other agreed price adjustments where appropriate. Consider a consent or no-renewal covenant before Completion if the commitments are material or outside the ordinary course.

- **Lease and Mossvale:** The materials identify a lease notification obligation and an assignment restriction, but do not establish that either requires consent merely because shares are sold. Do not assume a consent is required; verify the actual wording and obtain any required notice or consent before Completion. The Seller should not be able to treat a missing required notice as an immaterial disclosed matter.

- **Title:** The share register at DD-012 is evidence of the Seller’s recorded holding, not a substitute for the Seller’s warranty of good title. Require warranties that the Seller owns and can transfer 100% of the shares free of encumbrances, with all necessary corporate approvals and valid transfer documents at Completion. Do not subject title or capacity to the general cap, basket or 18-month period.

## Other drafting protections

The Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims. Reject that breadth. Preserve claims for fraud, deliberate concealment and other agreed carve-outs; ensure exclusive-remedy language does not displace specific indemnities or completion obligations. Any non-reliance clause should not undermine the express contractual warranties or remedies.

The Seller also says tax and IP positions are “settled” under the general regime. That is not a substitute for reviewing the actual warranty and indemnity wording. Seek tailored tax protection, including appropriate treatment of pre-Completion tax liabilities and claims, and IP warranties/indemnities addressing ownership, use, infringement and the Ironquay transfer issue.

## Summary of recommendations

Prioritise: **(1)** separate, stronger protection for fundamental and specific risks; **(2)** narrower disclosure and actual-knowledge exclusions; **(3)** pre-Completion Riverlark repayment and discharge; **(4)** Bluefen consent with all conditions satisfied as a true Completion condition; and **(5)** resolution of Ironquay IP, the export incident and omitted bonus liabilities. Then negotiate a longer and more workable claims regime, lower thresholds, tailored tax/IP protection, and verified treatment of supplier renewals and required notices.
=== END ADVICE ===
